The Lion Dance!
The lion dance comes from southern China. Two dancers become one lion, for good luck at the Lunar New Year.
Lion wakes up. Stand up and copy me!
Lion bows. Stand up and copy me!
The Jarabe Tapatio!
Folklorico dancers in Mexico dance the jarabe at fiestas. Their feet tap a rhythm on the floor.
Zapateado. Stand up and copy me!
Skirt swirl. Stand up and copy me!
The Irish Step Dance!
Irish dancers keep their arms still at their sides while their feet move fast. They dance at ceili parties.
Still arms, busy feet. Stand up and copy me!
Hop and kick. Stand up and copy me!
The Bhangra!
Bhangra comes from Punjab. Farmers danced it to celebrate the harvest, and people dance it at weddings and parties today.
Shoulder bounce. Stand up and copy me!
Bhangra hop. Stand up and copy me!
The Korean Fan Dance!
In the Korean fan dance, dancers open and close big painted fans. Together the fans look like flowers and waves.
Fan wave. Stand up and copy me!
Flower. Stand up and copy me!
The Second Line!
In New Orleans, people dance in the street behind a brass band. The dancers who follow the band are called the second line.
Strut. Stand up and copy me!
Umbrella twirl. Stand up and copy me!
The Kpanlogo!
Kpanlogo is a dance of the Ga people of Accra, Ghana. Drummers and dancers play together at celebrations.
Shoulder roll and arm swing. Stand up and copy me!
Low bounce. Stand up and copy me!
